description: NIFS is Gemini's near-infrared integral-field spectrograph. These six curves are the ZJ, JH and HK blocking filters, each scanned at room temperature and at 77 K.
facility_description: NIFS is used on the Gemini North 8.1 m telescope on Maunakea, operated by Gemini Observatory. It is an infrared integral-field spectrograph with a HAWAII-2RG detector.
notes: The components page says the gratings are used with one dual blocking filter: Z-J, J-H or H-K. The ZJ.dat header lists cut-on and cut-off at both temperatures and labels the columns 298 K and 77 K. The page also lists KG3 and KG5 neutral-density filters in the focal-plane unit; those are not these six bands. McGregor et al. 2003, Proc. SPIE 4841, is the instrument paper. The page describes the detector as a Rockwell HAWAII-2RG HgCdTe array and contrasts it with CCDs. No magnitude system is stated. DetectorType photon, DetectorTypeSource inferred (2026-10-26): no owner states the integration convention for the curve file, but the Gemini .dat files are witness scans of the blocking filters (HK.dat '#ED052-W H-K filter'), and the NIFS detector is a 'Rockwell HAWAII-2RG (H2RG)' HgCdTe device (https://www.gemini.edu/instrumentation/nifs/components), so the curves integrate as photon counters. SVO's energy label for HK and ZJ sits on identical arrays and gives no basis. The source is 'inferred' because this rests on the published curve content and the documented detector, not on an explicit owner statement.

ZJ_298K.Description: NIFS ZJ blocking filter at 298 K
ZJ_298K.Comments: Gemini filter table: ZJ, Gemini ID G0601, central wavelength 1.11 μm, coverage 0.77-1.44 μm. ZJ.dat's header names it the Z-J filter and gives two transmission columns, labelled 298 K and 77 K; this band is the 298 K column. The components page says the gratings are used with one dual blocking filter: Z-J, J-H or H-K.
